children: Zee Entertainment Enterprises Ltd shares fell over 6% on September 7 after The Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) has registered a case against promoter Subhash Chandra and others over alleged fraud involving more than Rs 1,322 crore in loans extended by LIC Housing Finance Ltd, according to an FIR registered on August 31.

The case follows a complaint by LIC Housing Finance alleging that Chandra, along with borrower companies and their directors, used false and inflated net-worth documents to secure loans from the home financier. The CBI has registered the case for criminal conspiracy, cheating and criminal breach of trust, among other offences.

LIC Housing Finance extended a Rs 500 crore loan to Vasant Sagar Properties Pvt Ltd and Pan India Infraprojects Pvt Ltd in March 2018 for business expansion. The loan was secured by a personal guarantee from Chandra.
On September 7, Zee shares closed over 6% lower at Rs 85.78 apiece.

In August 2018, the lender extended another Rs 480 crore to Digital Subscriber Management and Consultancy Services Pvt. Ltd and Spirit Infrapower and Multiventures Pvt. Ltd under a rental discounting facility. This loan was also secured by Chandra’s personal guarantee.

According to the complaint, the first loan was sanctioned partly on the basis of a net-worth certificate submitted by Chandra that put his net worth at $6.2 billion (Rs 59,113 crore) as of March 31, 2017. The second loan was sanctioned partly on the basis of another certificate stating his net worth at Rs 40,562 crore.

Both loan facilities subsequently went into default. The outstanding amount stood at Rs 570.50 crore for the Vasant Sagar facility and Rs 507.25 crore for the Digital loan, according to LIC Housing Finance’s complaint.

The complaint said Chandra later denied having the net worth stated in the certificates during personal insolvency proceedings. It said he reported his net worth in 2024 at Rs 31.79 crore and stated that it had not exceeded Rs 40,000 crore even in 2017-18.

LIC Housing Finance alleged that Chandra had acted in collusion with the borrower companies and their officers and directors to induce the lender to advance the loans. It also alleged that false documents were created to show an inflated net worth and that the borrowers subsequently misappropriated the funds.

The CBI has named Chandra, Vasant Sagar Properties, its director Pankaj Suroliya, Pan India Infraprojects, Digital Subscriber Management and Consultancy Services, its director Amish Pandya, Spirit Infrapower and Multiventures, its director Rajeev Dholakia, as well as unknown others and unknown public servants as accused.

title: Zee shares fall over 6% as CBI registers case against Subhash Chandra over alleged Rs 1,322-cr LIC Housing loan fraud
